title: [Platform] Noise rules: one open PR per routine, drafts, 7-day idle close
needs: G3 broker (GitHub scope of the rhino-ai-agents App); G3 Temporal namespace ai-agents
what: Build the PR rules every routine must pass: at most one open PR per routine, a routine:<name> label on each PR, every PR opens as a draft, and a routine PR with no activity for 7 days is closed with a note.
why: Our last dependency bot had 13 of 14 PRs closed unreviewed. These rules ship before any routine, so routines start quiet and earn attention instead of burning it.
how: Add orchestrator/src/activities/noise.ts to RhinoHealth/ai-agents with mayOpenPr and closeIdlePrs (sketch), plain async functions exported from activities/index.ts so the worker registers them. All GitHub calls go through the broker; the activity holds no token. Ask the broker owner (G3) for an orchestrator scope: read PRs, comment on and close PRs labelled routine:*.
mayOpenPr searches open PRs labelled routine:<name>. If one exists, the run waits and re-checks hourly with a Temporal timer instead of opening a second PR.
Every routine PR opens as a draft with the labels routine:<name> and agent. Marking it ready is G4's draft→ready step (green CI, nothing important open). This ticket never marks a PR ready.
closeIdlePrs runs daily from a Temporal schedule at an odd minute (23 3 * * *). Idle means no commit, comment or review for 7 days. It says why, closes the PR and comments on the linked Jira ticket.
Renovate PRs are out of scope here: Renovate manages its own PRs on its monthly schedule (G5-04).
Test with node:test (orchestrator/test/noise.test.ts) and a fake broker client over made-up PRs. No real repo in tests.

title: [Platform] Noise rules: daily team digest and auto-pause under 50% merged
needs: G3 Slack app (Bolt, Socket Mode) and the kill-switch flag store; G0 gateway spend tags
what: Post one Slack digest per team per day about its routines, and pause any routine when fewer than half of its last 20 closed PRs were merged.
why: One short message a day replaces many pings. A routine whose PRs people keep closing is noise, so it stops itself until its owner looks.
how: Add orchestrator/src/activities/digest.ts (sketch): one message per team (FE, BE, DevOps) with ready PRs waiting for review, drafts per owner, PRs closed as idle, paused routines with the reason, and yesterday's cost per routine from the gateway's spend tags.

Post it from the G3 Slack app to each team's channel, taken from config/people.yaml (G5-07). Schedule 37 6 * * 0-4 in Asia/Jerusalem (Sunday to Thursday). No message on a day with no routine activity.
mergeRate(routine): the last 20 closed PRs labelled routine:<name>, merged ÷ 20. With fewer than 20 there is no verdict, so a new routine is never paused on a handful of PRs.
Below 0.5: set routine:<name>:paused in the G3 flag store with the reason and DM the owner. Only the owner (or Sean) resumes it, with a Slack button.
The trust ladder (G5-15) reuses mergeRate for its demotion rule. Keep one function.

title: [BE] Renovate for fcp: grouped monthly updates; retire the weekly workflow
needs: DevOps: the rhino-actions-pr-creator App needs workflows: write (Action bumps) and Dependabot alerts: read (security PRs)
what: Run Renovate ourselves for fcp (npm, uv/pep621, the uv pip-compile files, base images, GitHub Actions) with grouped, monthly PRs and a 7-day minimum release age. Delete .github/workflows/weekly-dependency-upgrades.yml in the same PR.
why: Renovate stays a plain bot: fewer, grouped PRs, and nothing younger than a week. The upgrade fixers (G5-23, G5-24) repair only the PRs that break, so people see few dependency PRs, and green ones.
how: Add renovate.json5 at the fcp root (sketch; json5 so it can keep comments). It keeps today's scope and reviewers: frontend (frontend-guild), cloud/rhinoCloud, client and sdk (backend-guild), cloud/mcp-server (yaniv-rhino), cloud/connect-api (richard-engineering). ohif/ and cloud/rhinoCloud/rhino-containers/** stay out until the BE guild says otherwise.
fcp has no Terraform, and its one chart (client/.devops/charts/rhino-agent) has no dependencies, so the Terraform-provider and Helm rules live in G5-05.

Self-host it: add .github/workflows/renovate.yml on fcp-runner-set, cron 41 1 * * * (daily runs keep PRs rebased; new PRs appear only on the 1st), token from actions/create-github-app-token with RHINO_PR_CREATOR_APP_ID / RHINO_PR_CREATOR_PRIVATE_KEY, renovatebot/github-action pinned by SHA, RENOVATE_REPOSITORIES=RhinoHealth/fcp. Mend's hosted app can't run postUpgradeTasks, so self-hosting is required.

Allow only the post-upgrade commands in the sketch (global allowedCommands, env RENOVATE_ALLOWED_COMMANDS): make -C cloud/rhinoCloud update-deps keeps rhinoCore/integration-tests/requirements.txt in step, and the stub regeneration keeps gRPC in lockstep. Check the full Renovate image has uv and make.
Move the old workflow's 'gRPC versions match across client and cloud' Python check into cloud-ci's Lint job, so it guards Renovate and people alike.

Keep .github/dependabot.yml as it is (security alerts only, open-pull-requests-limit: 0). Renovate's vulnerabilityAlerts opens security fixes at once, outside the monthly schedule. frontend-ci runs only on pull_request, so leave prCreation at its default: the PR must exist for FE checks to run.
Dry run with RENOVATE_DRY_RUN=full and read the log before merging. Remove weekly-dependency-upgrades.yml in the same PR (no shim).

code.text:
// renovate.json5 (fcp root) — sketch. Replaces .github/workflows/weekly-dependency-upgrades.yml.
{
  $schema: "https://docs.renovatebot.com/renovate-schema.json",
  extends: ["config:recommended"],
  timezone: "Asia/Jerusalem",
  schedule: ["* 2-6 1 * *"],               // monthly: new PRs only on the 1st
  minimumReleaseAge: "7 days",
  internalChecksFilter: "strict",          // no branch at all until the release is 7 days old
  rangeStrategy: "update-lockfile",        // like `uv lock --upgrade` / `npm update`: stay inside our ranges
  lockFileMaintenance: { enabled: true },  // monthly refresh of transitive dependencies
  labels: ["dependencies"],
  prConcurrentLimit: 10,
  enabledManagers: ["npm", "pep621", "pip-compile", "dockerfile", "github-actions"],
  ignorePaths: ["**/node_modules/**", "ohif/**", "cloud/rhinoCloud/rhino-containers/**", "cloud/rhinoCloud/rhinoCore/integration-tests/**"],
  "pip-compile": { managerFilePatterns: ["/^sdk/requirements\\.txt$/", "/^cloud/mcp-server/requirements/.+\\.txt$/"] },
  packageRules: [
    { matchFileNames: ["frontend/**"], groupName: "frontend npm", reviewers: ["team:frontend-guild"] },
    { matchFileNames: ["cloud/rhinoCloud/**"], groupName: "cloud python", reviewers: ["team:backend-guild"],
      postUpgradeTasks: { executionMode: "branch", commands: ["make -C cloud/rhinoCloud update-deps"], fileFilters: ["cloud/rhinoCloud/**"] } },
    { matchFileNames: ["client/**"], groupName: "client python", reviewers: ["team:backend-guild"] },
    { matchFileNames: ["sdk/**"], groupName: "sdk python", reviewers: ["team:backend-guild"] },
    { matchFileNames: ["cloud/mcp-server/**"], groupName: "mcp-server", reviewers: ["yaniv-rhino"] },
    { matchFileNames: ["cloud/connect-api/**"], groupName: "connect-api python", reviewers: ["richard-engineering"] },
    { matchUpdateTypes: ["major"], groupName: null },   // one PR per major, so a fixer can take it alone
    { matchPackageNames: ["grpcio", "grpcio-tools", "grpcio-status", "grpcio-health-checking", "protobuf"],
      groupName: "grpc stack", reviewers: ["team:backend-guild"],   // client + cloud + stubs move together, majors too
      postUpgradeTasks: { executionMode: "branch", fileFilters: ["common/fcp_common/rhinoAgentRpc/**", "cloud/rhinoCloud/**"],
        commands: ["cd cloud/rhinoCloud && uv sync --frozen --no-install-project --only-group grpc-stub-gen && uv run --no-sync make -C ../../common/fcp_common/rhinoAgentRpc protoc",
                   "make -C cloud/rhinoCloud update-deps"] } },
    { matchManagers: ["github-actions"], groupName: "github actions" },
    { matchManagers: ["dockerfile"], groupName: "base images" },
    { matchPackageNames: ["RhinoHealth/byte"], enabled: false },   // Byte's own fleet sync pins it
  ],
}

title: [DevOps] Renovate for infrastructure and gitops: providers, charts, Actions
what: Run the same Renovate setup in the infrastructure repo (OpenTofu providers, tfr:/// modules, Helm chart versions in modules, Action SHAs, the runner image's base image) and in gitops (Helm chart dependencies, Action pins).
why: Provider, chart and Action updates are the infra side of the same noise problem. Grouped monthly PRs with a 7-day wait are easy to review, and the infra upgrade fixer (G5-32) repairs the ones that fail.
how: Add .github/renovate.json5 to infrastructure (sketch) and .github/workflows/renovate.yml on infrastructure-runner-set, the same shape as fcp's (G5-04), with actions pinned by SHA like the rest of the repo. Check which GitHub App may open PRs there; the PR-creator App may not be installed on infrastructure.

Providers are pinned inside a heredoc string in multi_tenant/common.hcl, single_tenant/common.hcl and terraform/accounts/common.hcl, so Renovate's Terraform manager can't see them. The first regex custom manager reads them. We run OpenTofu 1.12: check each bump also resolves on registry.opentofu.org.

Chart versions are module variable defaults (modules/n8n/variables.tf n8n_chart_version, modules/github-runner-scale-sets/variables.tf helm_chart_version). Add one line '# renovate: datasource=docker depName=<oci chart path>' above each default; the second custom manager reads them.

Infrastructure already pins Actions by SHA with a '# vX.Y.Z' comment through Dependabot (daily, 5-day cooldown). helpers:pinGitHubActionDigestsToSemver keeps that style. When Renovate's first Actions PR merges, remove the github-actions version-update block from .github/dependabot.yml (security alerts stay). Keep RhinoHealth/byte ignored.

gitops: .github/renovate.json5 with the helmv3 manager for Chart.yaml dependencies (for example cloud/temporal → temporal 1.5.0) and github-actions, on gitops-runner-set. Do not turn on helm-values: our own image tags in values files are written by the fcp publish jobs.
Infrastructure PRs keep their existing CODEOWNERS review (@RhinoHealth/devops). There is no plan in CI yet, so majors stay one PR each and a person runs the plan before merging.

code.text:
// infrastructure/.github/renovate.json5 — sketch. gitops gets the same base with helmv3 instead of the custom managers.
{
  $schema: "https://docs.renovatebot.com/renovate-schema.json",
  extends: ["config:recommended", "helpers:pinGitHubActionDigestsToSemver"],   // keeps the SHA + "# vX.Y.Z" style
  timezone: "Asia/Jerusalem",
  schedule: ["* 2-6 1 * *"],
  minimumReleaseAge: "7 days",
  internalChecksFilter: "strict",
  labels: ["dependencies"],                // CODEOWNERS already requests @RhinoHealth/devops here
  enabledManagers: ["custom.regex", "terragrunt", "github-actions", "dockerfile"],
  customManagers: [
    { // providers live in a heredoc in multi_tenant/, single_tenant/ and terraform/accounts/ common.hcl
      customType: "regex",
      managerFilePatterns: ["/(^|/)common\\.hcl$/"],
      matchStrings: ["source\\s*=\\s*\"(?<depName>[\\w-]+/[\\w-]+)\"\\s*\\n\\s*version\\s*=\\s*\"(?<currentValue>[\\d.]+)\""],
      datasourceTemplate: "terraform-provider",
    },
    { // chart versions are module variable defaults, each with a "# renovate:" line right above `default`
      customType: "regex",
      managerFilePatterns: ["/^modules/.+/variables\\.tf$/"],
      matchStrings: ["# renovate: datasource=(?<datasource>\\S+) depName=(?<depName>\\S+)\\s*\\n\\s*default\\s*=\\s*\"(?<currentValue>[^\"]+)\""],
    },
  ],
  packageRules: [
    { matchDatasources: ["terraform-provider"], groupName: "opentofu providers" },
    { matchManagers: ["terragrunt"], groupName: "registry modules" },          // tfr:/// sources in units
    { matchManagers: ["custom.regex"], matchDatasources: ["docker", "helm"], groupName: "helm charts" },
    { matchManagers: ["github-actions"], groupName: "github actions" },
    { matchPackageNames: ["RhinoHealth/byte"], enabled: false },
    { matchUpdateTypes: ["major"], groupName: null },   // majors one by one: a person reads the plan
  ],
}

title: [Platform] Routine charters: YAML format, loader and path limits in hooks
needs: G3 harness hooks (blockProtectedPaths) and the broker's git proxy; G0 locked checks; G8 skills
what: Define the charter every routine has (owner, trigger, allowed paths, never-list, skills, model, VM size, done), load it in the orchestrator, and enforce its paths with the harness hooks.
why: A charter turns 'Nova with a different trigger' into something concrete and reviewable. Paths are a wall, so they live in hooks and the broker, not in a prompt.
how: Add routines/charters/<name>.yaml to RhinoHealth/ai-agents, one file per routine, and a zod schema Charter in shared/src/schemas.ts (z.strictObject; the type comes from z.infer), read with the yaml package by orchestrator/src/routines/charter.ts. Reject unknown keys, more than 6 skills and an empty allowed_paths.
Load charters in an activity, loadCharter(name, sha), pinned to the ai-agents commit, so a Temporal replay sees the same charter.

Pass allowed_paths, denied_paths and never to the harness. Extend G3's blockProtectedPaths PreToolUse hook (a HookCallback in the harness that returns permissionDecision "deny") to refuse Edit and Write outside the allowed paths with a clear message; refusals are listed in the PR.

Bash can write files the hook can't see. Ask the broker owner (G3) to re-check the changed paths against the same charter at git push in the git proxy. That is the real wall; the hook gives an early, readable refusal.

Default paths per team: FE frontend/**; BE cloud/**, client/**, sdk/** with **/migrations/** denied in the pilot; DevOps the infrastructure and gitops repos plus .github/**. Lint, type and test config stay denied (G0 locked checks).
Write the first charter, fe-ci-fixer (sketch), and a node:test test (orchestrator/test/charters.test.ts) that loads every charter in CI.

Optional keys for routines outside fcp: repo (default RhinoHealth/fcp), read_only (extra read scopes for the broker) and setup (a command run in the VM before the session). The kb-ingest charter (G6-20) uses all three.

code.text:
# ai-agents/routines/charters/fe-ci-fixer.yaml — sketch; one file per routine, loaded by routineRun (G5-08)
name: fe-ci-fixer
team: fe
owner: from people.yaml              # never approves this routine's PRs (Requested-by: line, G5-07)
stage: shadow                        # shadow → drafts → normal (G5-15); promotions only by PR
trigger:
  kind: github.workflow_run
  repo: RhinoHealth/fcp
  workflows: ["[FRONTEND] - CI"]
  branch: main
  conclusion: failure
run_id: "cifix:fcp:{fingerprint}"    # one run per root cause (G5-09)
gather_minutes: 7                    # wait, then group (G5-17)
queue: cifix                         # task queue ai-agents-cifix; 2 VM slots (G3-25)
vm: { size: lite, spot: true }       # full when the failed job needs FCP Lab (jobs.yaml, G5-20)
model: { name: claude-opus-5-5, effort: low, on_failed_checks: medium }
allowed_paths: ["frontend/**"]       # PreToolUse hook, and again in the broker's git proxy at push
denied_paths: [".github/**", "frontend/biome.json", "frontend/tsconfig.json", "frontend/playwright.config.ts"]
never: [edit_test_assertions]        # on top of the false heals every routine is checked for (G5-14)
skills: [fix-ci, fe-codebase, verify, fcp-lab, pr-story]   # 5 of at most 6
done:
  - the failed job's commands fail on the red commit and pass on the fix, in the VM
  - npm run verify is green
  - no test weakened (false-heal check clean)
pr:
  title: "[FE] {jira}: fix red main: {summary}"
  labels: ["routine:fe-ci-fixer"]
  jira: create                       # a ticket is created or linked for every routine PR

title: [Guilds] Name routine owners and a reviewer of the day per team
needs: G0 independent-approval check (reads the Requested-by: line); G0 review rules agreed with Nir and Tal
what: Each guild names one owner per routine and a daily reviewer rotation. The owner is written as the requester on every PR of its routine, so the owner's approval never counts.
why: A routine needs a person who answers for it, and its PRs need a reviewer who did not ask for them. Exactly one approval, by someone who is not the requester, is a wall GitHub already enforces.
how: FE guild, BE guild and DevOps fill the teams block of config/people.yaml in ai-agents (sketch; the same file maps each person's Slack ID, Jira accountId and GitHub login for G4-05): an owner per routine, a reviewer rotation per team (GitHub handles) and the team's Slack channel for the digest.
Every routine PR body carries 'Requested-by: @<owner>'. G0's independent-approval check fails when the only approval is the requester's, so no new check is needed.

Reviewer of the day: the orchestrator picks rotation[workingDayIndex % rotation.length], skips the owner, and requests that one person when the PR is marked ready (stage normal). No CODEOWNERS file, no team-wide review request.

Agree how a Bug counts as triaged into a team. Today it is mixed: labels FE / frontend, title prefixes [FE] / [BE], components cloud / on-prem / infra, and the Team field (FE Guild, Infra Guild, squads). Proposal: the label FE or BE on a Bug in To Do. G5-13 uses the answer.
Swaps for holidays or sick days are a one-line PR to people.yaml. No calendar integration.

title: [Platform] routineRun workflow: Nova's harness driven by a charter
needs: G3 ticketToPr activities (acquireSandbox, workInSandbox, releaseSandbox), task queues with slots, kill switch; G4 scope judge, review panel, Byte on drafts, draft→ready
what: Build routineRun, the Temporal workflow every routine runs: load the charter, gather triggers, pass the gates, work in a fresh VM with Nova's harness, then ship through the same review layers as Nova, or save the result in shadow mode.
why: Routines must not fork Nova: same harness, same VMs, same walls, same review layers. Only the trigger and the charter differ, so safety is built once.
how: Add orchestrator/src/workflows/routine-run.ts (sketch). Reuse ticketToPr's activities unchanged. Extract the PR half of ticketToPr (scope judge with the charter, draft PR, Byte, fixing findings, ready) into a child workflow shipPr that both workflows use; agree the split with the G4 owner.
Signals: addTrigger (another event with the same root cause joins the run, G5-09) and decidePlan (the same Slack Approve / Change / Stop buttons as Nova).

preRunGate checks, in order: the G3 kill switch, routine:<name>:paused, incident mode (G5-17) and one open PR per routine (G5-02). A gate that says wait parks the run on a timer and never starts a VM.

TaskSpec.fromCharter builds the goal, done list, skills, paths, model and effort from the charter and the triggers. No maxTurns, no maxBudgetUsd, no taskBudget, no time limit: the 7-day activity timeout and 5-minute heartbeats only catch a dead worker.

Create or link the Jira ticket before the PR, so the title reads '[FE] RH-1234: …' and add-jira-links works. In shadow mode nothing is created: the diff and the proof go to S3 for the weekly comparison (G5-16).
Register keyword search attributes on namespace ai-agents: Routine, RunKind, RoutineOutcome, Stage. G5-17 and G5-21 query them.

Queues and slots as in G3-25: one task queue per routine family (ai-agents-cifix, ai-agents-upgrade, ai-agents-flaky, ai-agents-bugfix, ai-agents-health, ai-agents-security; a charter's queue key names it, and queueFor reads it) and VM slots per family (2, 2, 1, 2, 1, 1 to start) held by the slots workflow, not by routineRun.

title: [Platform] Start routine runs by root cause with signal-with-start
needs: G3 Temporal (namespace ai-agents), the broker's read-only GitHub scope, and the orchestrator service on inf-rhinohealth
what: Add the trigger service that turns an event into exactly one routineRun per root cause: it computes the workflow ID (the fingerprint) and uses signal-with-start, so a second event joins the open run.
why: When main goes red, every push and every PR fails the same way. One run per root cause is the first wall against a storm of agents.
how: Add orchestrator/src/triggers/github-events.ts (sketch) behind POST /v1/events in the orchestrator service on inf-rhinohealth (node:http, a small router, like Byte's broker). Internal only, no public route, so still no new public webhook.

Authenticate callers with GitHub OIDC: issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com, audience rhino-ai-agents, repository in an allow-list, job_workflow_ref equal to the trigger workflow on main (G5-12). The runner holds no Temporal credential.
Never trust the request body: re-read the run by run_id through the broker (read-only, actions: read) to get the failing jobs and the first error line of each job's log.

IDs: cifix:<repo>:<fingerprint> for red main; upgrade:<repo>:pr-<n> for a failed Renovate PR; bugfix:RH-1234 for bugs (G5-13); sched:<name> for schedules. The fingerprint is the last green commit of that workflow on main, the failing job names and each job's normalized first error. The last green commit doesn't move while main stays red, so later pushes join the same run.

client.workflow.signalWithStart, the signal-with-start form of G3-25's startRun (same <agent>:<thing> ID, queue ai-agents-<agent> and Agent search attribute, so the kill switch's batch stop finds these runs; put it in fanout.ts with the G3 owner), with workflowIdReusePolicy REJECT_DUPLICATE: a root cause that comes back after its run closed goes to a person in #ai-agents-alerts (likely ping-pong), never to a new run. Namespace retention bounds how long an ID is remembered.
Unit-test fingerprint and normalize with node:test (orchestrator/test/github-events.test.ts) on 10 saved logs from real red builds (G5-11): the same failure on two commits must give the same ID.

title: [Platform] ROUTINE-BENCH: case format, runner and per-routine score
needs: G4 TICKET-BENCH runner (Harbor on the sandbox image) and its restricted golden-set repo; G1 eval results store
what: Define one case format for every routine slice, turn cases into Harbor tasks, run each case 3 times, and score each routine's slice.
why: A routine leaves shadow only when its slice passes, and every skill or charter change re-runs that slice. One format keeps the slices comparable and cheap to grow.
how: Add evals/routine-bench/<slice>/<case-id>/case.yaml to ai-agents (sketch). Golden data (logs, human fixes, hidden tests) lives in the restricted golden-set repo that G4 sets up for TICKET-BENCH, never in ai-agents itself.

Write evals/routine-bench/to_harbor.py: one Harbor task per case (the instruction is the trigger, the environment is the sandbox image at base_commit, the tests are the grade block). Reuse the G4 runner; don't build a second one.

Grading: must_pass commands green; hidden tests from the human fix copied in only at grading time; the false-heal check (G5-14) clean; changed paths inside the charter. For bug fixers, reproduced means the routine's new test fails on base and passes with the human fix.
Score per slice: solved rate (pass@1 and pass^3), reproduce rate, false heals, cost and minutes per case. Time and cost are measured, never limits. Results go as JSON to the G1 eval results store.
CI in ai-agents: a change to routines/charters/<name>.yaml or to that routine's skills re-runs its slice and posts the score on the PR.
Data rule for every case: fake seed data only, saved logs scrubbed with gitleaks, no customer text.

code.text:
# ai-agents/evals/routine-bench/red-builds/fe-ci-0412/case.yaml — sketch; every slice uses this shape
id: fe-ci-0412
routine: fe-ci-fixer
slice: red-builds
cause: code                         # code | test | environment | flaky (environment cases expect hand_off)
repo: RhinoHealth/fcp
base_commit: "<sha of the first red commit>"
trigger:                            # exactly what the routine would have received (G5-09)
  kind: github.workflow_run
  workflow: "[FRONTEND] - CI"
  failed_jobs: ["Unit Tests"]
  log: golden://red-builds/fe-ci-0412/failed.log   # restricted golden-set repo, scrubbed with gitleaks
reference:
  human_fix: "<sha of the next green commit>"      # for the comparison only, never shown to the agent
grade:
  expect: fix                       # fix | hand_off | reproduce_only
  must_pass:
    - cd frontend && npm ci && npm run check-types && npm run lint && npm run test:unit
  hidden_tests: []                  # bug and upgrade cases copy the human PR's tests in at grading time
  reproduced: null                  # bug cases: the routine's test fails on base and passes on human_fix
  false_heal: reject                # G5-14 runs on the diff; any finding fails the case
  allowed_paths: ["frontend/**"]    # from the routine's charter
runs: 3                             # pass@1 and pass^3; cost and minutes recorded, never limited

title: [Platform] ROUTINE-BENCH slice: 30 past red builds on main
what: Collect 30 past red builds of fcp's main (frontend-ci, cloud-ci, client-ci), each with the commit that turned it green, as cases for the FE and BE CI fixers.
why: The CI fixers stay in shadow until they solve at least half of this slice with zero false heals.
how: Write evals/routine-bench/collect_red_builds.py (sketch): list failed runs on main per workflow with gh, keep the first red of each red streak, find the next green run, save the failed jobs' logs and the fix commit.
GitHub keeps Actions logs for about 90 days, so collect now. For older reds, rebuild the case by running the failed job's commands at the red commit in a VM.
Label each case by cause: code, test, environment (QA lock, runner, registry) or flaky. Environment cases expect hand_off, not a fix.
Aim for about 12 frontend, 12 cloud and 6 client cases. Drop cases with the same fingerprint (same root cause).
A BE engineer checks each cloud and client case: is the next green commit really the fix, and does must_pass really prove it?

title: [Platform] Trigger Action on fcp-runner-set: red main, failed Renovate PRs
needs: G3 orchestrator reachable from the runner pods in inf-rhinohealth
what: Add a small workflow to fcp that runs on workflow_run when a CI workflow fails on main or on a renovate/* branch, and sends the run ID to the trigger service.
why: GitHub events are how the CI and upgrade fixers wake up. A tiny Action on our own runners, with no secrets and no PR code, is the safest bridge.
how: Add .github/workflows/ai-agents-routine-trigger.yml (sketch). It runs on fcp-runner-set, which lives in inf-rhinohealth, so it reaches the internal trigger service. Set the repo variable AI_AGENTS_TRIGGER_URL.

It never checks out code and never puts event fields into a shell; it reads them in JS from context.payload, so nothing can be injected. Permissions: id-token: write (for the OIDC token) and contents: read.

Watched workflows: [FRONTEND] - CI, [CLOUD] - CI, [CLIENT] - CI, [SDK] - CI. Cloud, client and SDK CI run on push to every branch, so Renovate branches get checks without a PR; frontend CI runs on pull_request.

A workflow_run workflow only fires from the default branch's copy. Test it after merge with a planted failure on a throwaway branch named renovate/test-trigger while every routine is in shadow (nothing gets opened).

Copy the file into infrastructure (infrastructure-runner-set, watching [TERRAGRUNT] Lint and the other check workflows) and gitops (gitops-runner-set) for the pipeline fixer (G5-25), and add both repos to the trigger service's OIDC allow-list.
This Action only reports. The orchestrator never calls workflow_dispatch and never re-runs jobs.

code.text:
# .github/workflows/ai-agents-routine-trigger.yml (fcp) — sketch
name: "[AI-AGENTS] - Routine trigger"
on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ["[FRONTEND] - CI", "[CLOUD] - CI", "[CLIENT] - CI", "[SDK] - CI"]
    types: [completed]

permissions:
  id-token: write   # the OIDC token proves "this workflow, in RhinoHealth/fcp" to the trigger service
  contents: read

jobs:
  report:
    if: >-
      github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'failure' &&
      (github.event.workflow_run.head_branch == 'main' ||
       startsWith(github.event.workflow_run.head_branch, 'renovate/'))
    runs-on: fcp-runner-set   # inside inf-rhinohealth, so it reaches the internal trigger service
    steps:
      # No checkout and no ${{ }} inside the script: event fields are read in JS, so nothing can be injected.
      - uses: actions/github-script@v9   # pin by SHA with the rest of the Actions (G5-04)
        env:
          TRIGGER_URL: ${{ vars.AI_AGENTS_TRIGGER_URL }}
        with:
          script: |
            const run = context.payload.workflow_run
            const token = await core.getIDToken("rhino-ai-agents")
            const res = await fetch(`${process.env.TRIGGER_URL}/v1/events`, {
              method: "POST",
              headers: {authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, "content-type": "application/json"},
              body: JSON.stringify({kind: "github.workflow_run", repo: context.repo.repo, run_id: run.id})
            })
            if (!res.ok) core.setFailed(`trigger service answered ${res.status}`)

title: [Platform] Jira Bug and Temporal schedule triggers for routines
needs: G4 Jira poller (Temporal schedule, JQL every minute); the broker's Jira scope; Security (Ronen) for the customer-data label
what: Start bug fixers from triaged Bug tickets through the existing Jira poller, and start the scheduled routines and housekeeping jobs (dead code, digest, idle close, ladder, shadow report) from Temporal schedules at odd minutes.
why: Bug tickets are the most important trigger, and schedules drive the daily and weekly crews. Reusing the poller keeps us at zero new public webhooks.
how: Add the routine schedules to orchestrator/src/triggers/schedules.ts (sketch; the file G3-28 creates for the Jira polls) as ensureCronSchedules(), called when the worker starts next to G3-28's ensureSchedules(). It is safe to run twice: an existing schedule is updated.

Register the bug JQL in G3-28's query registry, every 5 minutes (enough for bugs): Bugs in To Do, unassigned, with the team label agreed in G5-07. Each match starts bugfix:RH-1234 on the ai-agents-bugfix queue through startRun (G3-25), so a repeat poll is a no-op.
Skip tickets labelled no-routine (anyone can opt a bug out). When a person takes the ticket during a run (the assignee changes), send a stop signal: the run posts what it found and ends.

PHI never enters a prompt: the broker's Jira scope returns summary, description and comments only, never attachments (screenshots, logs). Agree with Security (Ronen) on a label that keeps a ticket away from agents when it might hold customer data, and add it to the JQL.
Schedules use client.schedule.create with ScheduleOverlapPolicy.SKIP and the Asia/Jerusalem time zone. Weekly code-health routines run on Sunday.

title: [Platform] False-heal check: reject weakened tests in routine PRs
needs: G0-19 weakened-tests detector (deleted assertions, new skips, loosened thresholds); G4 scope judge
what: Add the check that runs on every routine diff before the scope judge and rejects false heals: deleted or skipped tests, removed assertions, loosened thresholds, and anything the charter's never-list forbids.
why: A CI fixer can always turn CI green by weakening a test. That is the one failure that must never ship, and one false heal moves a routine back a step on the trust ladder.
how: Add harness/src/checks/false-heal.ts (sketch). Build on G0-19's weakened-tests detector (ai-agents/checks/src/weakened-tests.ts): one implementation, with the charter rules added here.
For Nova these findings are flags in the PR. For routines any finding rejects the run (outcome false_heal), and the scope judge gets the list together with the charter.

Charter rules: edit_test_assertions (CI fixers may not touch an existing assertion), add_code (dead-code removers may only delete; an import line that only loses names is fine), add_retries_or_sleeps (flaky-test fixer).

Patterns cover both stacks: pytest and unittest skips and xfail, Vitest and Playwright .skip / .only / fixme, assert / self.assert* / expect(, and thresholds (fail-under, Playwright retries, timeouts).
Also run it in the VM from the Stop hook, so the agent sees the problem before it calls itself done.
node:test cases (harness/test/false-heal.test.ts) from real diffs: one honest fix, one deleted test, one it.skip, one lowered --fail-under, one added time.sleep.

title: [Platform] Trust ladder: shadow, drafts to the owner, normal
needs: G1 eval results store (bench scores)
what: Give every routine a stage (shadow → drafts to the owner → normal), with automatic demotion and owner-signed promotion.
why: Routines earn trust from evidence. A routine moves up only when its bench slice passes with zero false heals, and moves back a step as soon as it misbehaves.
how: Stages: shadow runs on real triggers and opens nothing. Drafts opens real draft PRs and pings only the owner; the owner may mark a good one ready, which sends it to the reviewer of the day. Normal marks clean PRs ready and requests the reviewer of the day.
Add orchestrator/src/routines/ladder.ts (sketch) and a daily schedule that evaluates every routine (G5-13).

Demote one step on any false heal, on a revert of one of its PRs within 14 days (a 'Revert "…"' commit on main naming the PR), or when under half of its last 20 PRs merged (mergeRate from G5-03). Demotion is immediate: write routine:<name>:stage_override in the flag store, then open a PR that lowers stage: in the charter, so the file stays the truth.

Promote only through a PR that raises stage: in the charter. The daily job DMs the owner when the routine qualifies: slice solved at least 50% (bug fixers also reproduce at least 60%), zero false heals, at least 10 runs at the current stage. The owner opens or asks for that PR; someone else approves it.
The effective stage is the lower of the charter and the override. routineRun reads it at start and stores it in the Stage search attribute.

title: [Platform] Weekly shadow report: the routine's fix vs the human fix
needs: G1 weekly run review
what: Each week, compare every shadow run's saved fix with what a person actually did for the same failure or bug, and post a short table to the weekly run review.
why: Shadow mode helps only if someone looks at it. This report shows each owner whether the routine would have helped, before it opens anything.
how: Add orchestrator/src/reports/shadow-report.ts (sketch), run by the Sunday schedule (G5-13).
Find the human fix: for red main, the commits between the red run and the next green one; for bugs, the merged PR linked to the ticket; for upgrades, what the Renovate PR became.
If the human fix added tests, run them on the routine's saved diff in a lite VM. That is the objective answer to 'would it have worked'.
A Sonnet 5.5 judge at medium effort with a short rubric answers: same root cause? smaller or bigger change? would a reviewer reject it? Check the judge on 10 labelled pairs first.
Post one row per run (routine, trigger, human PR, tests passed, verdict, cost) to the weekly run review thread. Nothing goes to the team channels.

title: [Platform] Storm control: gather window and incident mode for red main
needs: G3 kill-switch flag store; DevOps: a PagerDuty service for ai-agents
what: When main goes red, wait about 7 minutes so failures gather into one run per root cause, and switch to incident mode (fixers paused, a person paged) when more than 5 new fingerprints appear in 15 minutes.
why: Many new failures at once mean an infrastructure problem (runners, registry, QA), not code. Agents can't fix that, and a storm of fix runs only costs money and attention.
how: CI and pipeline-fixer charters set gather_minutes: 7. routineRun sleeps that long before its gate while addTrigger signals pile up (G5-08).

Add orchestrator/src/activities/storm.ts (sketch). stormCheck counts cifix runs started in the last 15 minutes with a Temporal visibility query (client.workflow.count) on the Routine and RunKind search attributes.

Over 5: set routines:fixers:paused with the reason, page the on-call person through PagerDuty (ask DevOps for an ai-agents service), and post the fingerprints and their first error lines to #ai-agents-alerts. Page once per incident, not once per run.
While paused, new cifix runs park at the gate. A person clears the flag with a Slack button; the parked runs re-check, and most find main green and end as not_needed.
After the gather window, a run first checks that main is still red at its latest commit (stillRed). If it is green, the run ends with nothing to do.
Test with a replay in a test namespace: 8 saved red-build events in 2 minutes must give one page and zero VMs.

title: [BE] ROUTINE-BENCH slice: 20 broken dependency updates
what: Collect 20 dependency updates (npm and Python) that broke CI or needed code changes, each with the human repair, as cases for the FE and BE upgrade fixers.
why: The upgrade fixers are tuned on real failures first, and leave shadow only when they solve at least half of this slice.
how: Sources: the 'Weekly dependency upgrade: …' PRs that failed CI (label dependencies), and merged PRs that changed frontend/package.json or a uv.lock together with source files (the human repair).
Each case is a replay: only the bump (manifest and lockfile) on the base commit. The human's source changes are the reference fix, and the tests they added become hidden tests.
Mix: about 10 npm (frontend), 8 Python (cloud, client, sdk) and 2 grouped updates where only one package breaks, to test the per-package pipeline (G5-23).
Leave gRPC and protobuf bumps out: they touch the cloud↔client contract, which goes to people.
Write each case as case.yaml (sketch) and check it builds as a Harbor task (G5-10).

code.text:
# ai-agents/evals/routine-bench/broken-updates/fe-npm-0031/case.yaml — sketch of an upgrade case
id: fe-npm-0031
routine: fe-upgrade-fixer
slice: broken-updates
repo: RhinoHealth/fcp
base_commit: "<main sha before the human repair>"
trigger:
  kind: renovate_pr_failed
  workflow: "[FRONTEND] - CI"
  failed_jobs: ["Unit Tests"]
  bump:                                    # replayed on base: manifest + lockfile only
    - { package: "<npm package>", from: "<old>", to: "<new major>" }
  group: ["<another package in the same group>"]   # 2 cases are groups where only one package breaks
reference:
  human_fix: "<merge sha of the PR that repaired our code>"
  changelog: "<link to the package's migration guide>"
grade:
  expect: fix
  must_pass:
    - cd frontend && npm ci && npm run check-types && npm run lint && npm run test:unit && npm run build
  hidden_tests: ["<tests the human PR added>"]
  false_heal: reject
  allowed_paths: ["frontend/**"]
  pinned_back: fail                        # pinning the old version again is not a fix
runs: 3

title: [Guilds] ROUTINE-BENCH slice: 30 past FE and BE bugs with their tests
needs: Security (Ronen): read the ticket text of each case for customer data
what: Pick 30 bugs that people fixed in 2025–26 (about 15 FE and 15 BE) where the fixing PR added a test, and turn them into cases for the bug fixers.
why: The bug fixers are the most important routines. They leave shadow only when they reproduce at least 60% of these bugs and solve at least half.
how: Mine candidates with evals/routine-bench/collect_bugs.py (sketch): Done Bugs in project RH, linked to a merged fcp PR (the RH key in the PR title, as add-jira-links does) that changed test files.
Each guild reviews its candidates and keeps bugs whose ticket text alone is enough to start (no hidden chat context) and whose test really checks the bug.
A case is: the ticket summary and description as the trigger (no attachments), base = the PR's merge base, hidden tests = the PR's test files, reference fix = the PR's source changes.
Reproduce grading: the routine's own regression test must fail on base and pass with the human fix applied. That shows it found the same bug, not a different one.
FE cases run on a full VM with FCP Lab and seed data from TestDataCreator; BE cases run the cloud or client unit tests.
No customer data in cases: read each ticket before it goes in, and drop any that names a customer, a site or real records.

code.text:
# ai-agents/evals/routine-bench/collect_bugs.py — sketch: candidates only; each guild picks its final 15
JQL = 'project = RH AND issuetype = Bug AND status = Done AND resolved >= "2025-01-01" ORDER BY resolved DESC'
TEST_PATH = re.compile(r"(^|/)(tests?|e2e)/|test_[^/]*\.py$|\.(test|spec)\.tsx?$")
BE_PATHS = ("cloud/", "client/", "sdk/")


def candidates(jira: Jira, gh: GitHub) -> Iterator[dict]:
    for issue in jira.search(JQL, fields=["summary", "description"]):  # text only, never attachments
        for pr in gh.search_prs("RhinoHealth/fcp", f'"{issue.key}" in:title is:merged'):  # add-jira-links style
            files = gh.pr_files(pr.number)
            tests = [f for f in files if TEST_PATH.search(f)]
            source = [f for f in files if f not in tests]
            if not tests or not source or len(source) > 8:  # needs a test and a reviewable fix
                continue
            if all(f.startswith("frontend/") for f in source):
                team = "fe"
            elif all(f.startswith(BE_PATHS) for f in source):
                team = "be"
            else:
                continue  # cross-tier fixes are not bug-fixer work
            yield {"id": issue.key.lower(), "team": team,
                   "ticket": {"summary": issue.summary, "description": issue.description},
                   "base_commit": gh.merge_base(pr), "human_fix": pr.merge_commit_sha, "hidden_tests": tests,
                   "review": ["customer data in the text?", "is the ticket enough on its own?"]}

title: [Platform] FE CI fixer: one fix run when frontend-ci goes red on main
needs: G8 fix-ci and fe-codebase skills; G7 npm run verify; G3 Nexus npm proxy
what: Turn on the first routine: when [FRONTEND] - CI fails on main, one run per root cause reproduces the failing job in a VM, makes the smallest fix inside frontend/, and proves main's checks pass with no test weakened.
why: Red main blocks everyone. A quick, honest fix, or a clear hand-off when it's the environment, shortens red-main time, one of this goal's done-when numbers.
how: Use the fe-ci-fixer charter (G5-06), stage shadow. Skills fix-ci, fe-codebase, verify, fcp-lab, pr-story. Opus 5.5 at low effort; a failed step re-runs at medium. Lite Spot VM; full only for e2e failures.
Add routines/fe-ci-fixer/jobs.yaml (sketch): how each frontend-ci job is reproduced in the VM, and which jobs are hand-offs.
First step is always 'is it us?': run the failed commands at main's head in the VM. Green in the VM means environment or flake: post the evidence to #ai-agents-alerts and stop.
The fix must pass npm run verify (G7) and the reproduced job's commands. The false-heal check (G5-14) and the scope judge run before any PR.
Tune on 5 cases from the red-builds slice (G5-11), then run the full FE part of the slice 3 times before turning on shadow.

code.text:
# ai-agents/routines/fe-ci-fixer/jobs.yaml — sketch: how each "[FRONTEND] - CI" job is reproduced in the VM
workflow: "[FRONTEND] - CI"
setup: cd frontend && npm ci                     # Node 24.15; packages through the Nexus npm proxy (G3)
check_main_first: true                           # failed commands green at main's head → environment or flake
jobs:
  "Unit Tests":
    vm: lite
    repro:
      - .github/scripts/frontend/script-tests/test-playwright-parallelism.sh
      - cd frontend && npm run check-types
      - cd frontend && npm run lint
      - cd frontend && npm run test:unit
  "Build":
    vm: lite
    repro: ["cd frontend && npm run build", "cd frontend && npm run build-storybook"]
  "Build E2E app":
    vm: full
    repro: ["<copy the build steps from .github/workflows/_frontend-build-e2e-app.yml>"]
  "I&T - AWS":
    vm: full
    repro: ["cd frontend && npx playwright test --project=pr <failed spec>   # against FCP Lab, not QA"]
    if_green_in_lab: hand_off                    # passes on Lab, failed on QA → QA env or data, not code
  "I&T - GCP": { same_as: "I&T - AWS" }
  "Deploy": { hand_off: "needs cloud credentials; DevOps" }
  "Publish": { hand_off: "image publishing; DevOps" }

title: [Platform] Circuit breaker: pause a routine when 3 of its last 5 runs fail
what: After every run, look at the routine's last 5 finished runs. If 3 failed or were rejected, pause the routine and tell its owner.
why: A routine that keeps failing wastes VMs and reviewer time. Pausing it fast, with the reasons attached, is cheaper than a slow drift into noise.
how: routineRun sets RoutineOutcome when it ends: merged, closed, rejected (scope-judge veto, false heal, closed by a person), failed (no fix), handed_off, not_needed.
Add circuitBreaker to orchestrator/src/activities/storm.ts (sketch) and call it as the last step of every run.
Only failed and rejected count. handed_off (environment problems) and not_needed are not the routine's fault.
On trip: set routine:<name>:paused, DM the owner the 5 runs and their reasons, and list it in the next team digest. Resuming is a Slack button for the owner.
Ping-pong is already covered: a fingerprint that comes back after its run closed is refused by REJECT_DUPLICATE (G5-09) and goes to a person.

title: [Platform] BE CI fixer: one fix run when cloud-ci or client-ci goes red
needs: G8 be-codebase skill; G7 poe verify
what: Reuse the FE CI fixer for [CLOUD] - CI and [CLIENT] - CI on main: reproduce the failed job, fix it inside cloud/, client/ or sdk/, and prove it without weakening a test.
why: Backend red builds block the same people. The flow is the same as FE; only the commands, paths and skills change.
how: Charter be-ci-fixer, stage shadow: paths cloud/**, client/**, sdk/**, with **/migrations/** denied; skills fix-ci, be-codebase, verify, fcp-lab, pr-story; Opus 5.5 low, re-run at medium; lite Spot VM, full when tests need the compose services.
Add routines/be-ci-fixer/jobs.yaml (sketch) mapping cloud-ci and client-ci jobs to VM commands.

Hand off, don't fix: protoc drift (the stubs live in common/fcp_common/, outside BE routine paths, and are the cloud↔client contract), a makemigrations --check failure (no migrations in the pilot), and I&T failures that need the QA envs.
Run the BE part of the red-builds slice (G5-11) 3 times before turning on shadow.

code.text:
# ai-agents/routines/be-ci-fixer/jobs.yaml — sketch: "[CLOUD] - CI" and "[CLIENT] - CI" jobs in the VM
check_main_first: true
workflows:
  "[CLOUD] - CI":
    "Lint":
      vm: lite
      repro:
        - cd cloud/rhinoCloud && uv sync --frozen --only-group lint --no-install-project
        - pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure
      hand_off_if: "the diff is in common/fcp_common/rhinoAgentRpc (protoc drift: the cloud↔client contract)"
    "Unit Tests":
      vm: full                                   # postgres, minio and redis come from the compose services
      repro:
        - ./scripts/local_run_backend_unit_tests.sh cloud <failed test label>
        - ./scripts/local_run_backend_unit_tests.sh cloud    # the whole suite before "done"
      hand_off_if: "makemigrations --dry-run --check fails (no migrations in the pilot)"
    "I&T - AWS": { hand_off: "runs on qa-cloud behind cloud_integration_tests_aws; the VM has no QA access" }
    "I&T - GCP": { hand_off: "same, behind cloud_integration_tests_gcp" }
    "Publish": { hand_off: "edits RhinoHealth/gitops; DevOps" }
  "[CLIENT] - CI":
    "Lint":
      vm: lite
      repro:
        - cd client/rhinoOnPrem && uv sync --frozen --only-group lint --no-install-project
        - pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure
    "Unit Tests": { vm: full, repro: ["./scripts/local_run_backend_unit_tests.sh client <failed test label>"] }
    "I&T - AWS": { hand_off: "qa-on-prem behind client_integration_tests_aws" }
    "I&T - GCP": { hand_off: "behind client_integration_tests_gcp" }

title: [Platform] FE upgrade fixer: repair failed npm Renovate PRs per package
needs: G8 upgrade-dependency skill; G3 Nexus npm proxy
what: When frontend-ci fails on a Renovate PR, find which package in the group breaks the build, fix our code for that package, and push small commits to the Renovate branch.
why: Grouped monthly updates stay quiet only if the broken ones get repaired. Airbnb's step-by-step pipelines with retries show that one small pipeline per unit beats one big agent session.
how: Charter fe-upgrade-fixer, stage shadow: paths frontend/**; skills upgrade-dependency, fe-codebase, verify, fcp-lab, pr-story; Opus 5.5 low, re-run at medium; full Spot VM, because the flows that use the package are checked in the browser.

Add harness/src/routines/upgrades.ts (sketch; it runs inside the VM, so it lives in the harness, not in routines/), shared with the BE fixer: try each bump alone on the base commit, then run one fix session per breaking package, then check all fixes together on the Renovate branch.
Each fix session reads the changelog and migration guide, searches our usage, tries the package's codemod if it has one, and runs the e2e specs and stories that use the package.

Push the fix commits to the Renovate branch through the broker's git proxy (that branch only). Renovate sees an edited branch and stops rebasing it, which is what we want. Add the routine:fe-upgrade-fixer label and the owner's Requested-by: line.
A package it can't fix: comment on the PR what breaks and why, and leave the decision to a person. Never pin the old version back as a 'fix'.
Tune on 5–10 real failures from the broken-updates slice (G5-18) before shadow.

title: [Platform] BE upgrade fixer: repair a failed Python Renovate PR
needs: G7 poe verify, oasdiff and the SDK smoke test
what: Reuse the per-package pipeline for Python Renovate PRs (cloud, client, sdk) that fail CI, with the SDK and API checks added to done.
why: Python bumps can break the API or the published SDK quietly. The fixer proves both still work before a person sees the PR.
how: Add the be-upgrade-fixer charter (sketch), stage shadow.

Bump one package at a time: uv lock --upgrade-package in the app's folder, then make update-deps for cloud so the integration-tests requirements stay in step; for sdk, uv pip compile with --upgrade-package.
Done: the failing workflow green on the branch, the SDK tests green (make -C sdk test), and the OpenAPI diff (G7) showing no unplanned API change.
gRPC and protobuf bumps are handed to the BE guild with the failure; the routine never fixes them.

code.text:
# ai-agents/routines/charters/be-upgrade-fixer.yaml — sketch
name: be-upgrade-fixer
team: be
stage: shadow
trigger:
  kind: github.workflow_run
  repo: RhinoHealth/fcp
  workflows: ["[CLOUD] - CI", "[CLIENT] - CI", "[SDK] - CI"]
  branch: "renovate/*"
  conclusion: failure
run_id: "upgrade:fcp:pr-{pr_number}"           # one run per Renovate PR
queue: upgrade                             # 2 slots
vm: { size: full, spot: true }
model: { name: claude-opus-5-5, effort: low, on_failed_checks: medium }
allowed_paths: ["cloud/**", "client/**", "sdk/**"]
denied_paths: ["**/migrations/**", "common/**"]
never: [edit_test_assertions]
hand_off:
  - packages: [grpcio, grpcio-tools, grpcio-status, grpcio-health-checking, protobuf]   # cloud↔client contract
    to: backend-guild
bump_cmd:
  cloud/rhinoCloud: "uv lock --upgrade-package {package} && make update-deps"
  client/rhinoOnPrem: "uv lock --upgrade-package {package}"
  sdk: "uv pip compile pyproject.toml --python-version 3.13 --extra lint --extra test --extra docs --no-strip-extras --upgrade-package {package} -o requirements.txt"
skills: [upgrade-dependency, be-codebase, verify, fcp-lab, pr-story]
done:
  - the Renovate PR's failing workflow is green on the branch
  - make -C sdk test is green and the OpenAPI diff shows no unplanned change (G7)
  - no test weakened (G5-14)
pr: { labels: ["routine:be-upgrade-fixer"], requested_by: owner }

title: [DevOps] Pipeline fixer: red workflows in infrastructure, gitops, .github
needs: G3 lite image with tofu, terragrunt, tflint, trivy, helm, kubeconform, actionlint and zizmor; G7 DevOps checks; Security (Ronen) on the workflows permission
what: Turn on the DevOps pipeline fixer: when a check workflow fails on main in infrastructure or gitops, or a workflow file breaks, one run reproduces it on a lite VM and proposes a fix with the check output. A person applies anything that touches cloud resources.
why: DevOps checks are growing (G7), and red pipelines block everyone. The fixer works with no cloud credentials and never applies, destroys, syncs or dispatches.
how: Charter pipeline-fixer, stage shadow: the infrastructure and gitops repos plus .github/** in fcp; skills fix-ci, devops-codebase, infra-change, verify, pr-story; never tofu/terraform apply or destroy, argocd app sync, or workflow_dispatch. title: [Platform] Bug fixers: triage, reproduce first, fix with a proven test
needs: G4 plan step and the Slack Approve / Change / Stop buttons; G8 fix-bug and kb skills
what: Build the bug-fixer flow both teams share: triage the ticket, reproduce first, find the root cause with file:line, make the smallest fix, and prove the regression test fails without the fix and passes with it. Bigger fixes wait for plan approval; bugs it can't reproduce get a clear ticket update.
why: Reproduce-first is what makes an agent's bug fix trustworthy (Agentless and SWE-agent both work this way). A failed reproduction, written up well, is useful on its own.
how: Triage with Sonnet 5.5 at low effort and a structured answer: a duplicate of an open ticket? the right team? how bad? Wrong team → comment and stop.

Reproduce with Opus 5.5 at high effort: a failing test or a recorded browser run on seed data. If it can't, it comments on the ticket: the steps tried, the seed data and commands used, what is missing (role, data shape, browser, exact steps) and one specific question. Outcome handed_off.

Plan: the root cause with file:line and why it happened. If the fix is more than a small, local change (the agent judges, using the fix-bug skill), the plan goes to the ticket owner (the person who triaged it, or the routine owner) with Approve / Change / Stop, and the run waits on decidePlan.

Proof before done (sketch, proveRegressionTest): the new test runs on the base commit with only the test files added and must fail on behaviour, then on the fix and must pass. The Stop hook asks for evidence until both hold.
Look for the same pattern nearby and list it in the PR; fix only the reported bug.
When the PR opens, assign the ticket to the routine owner so a person owns it, and comment with the PR link and the proof.

why: Most FE bugs are visible behaviour. A recorded run that fails before and passes after is proof any reviewer can check in 30 seconds.
how: Charter fe-bug-fixer, stage shadow: paths frontend/**; skills fix-bug, fe-codebase, verify, fcp-lab, pr-story, kb (6); Opus 5.5 at high effort; full on-demand VM (it waits on people, so no Spot).

Regression specs follow frontend/AGENTS.md (sketch): page objects in e2e/pages, test.step Given / When / Then, assertions on test IDs, ARIA and visible text. A missing locator becomes a page-object method first.
Layout bugs are checked at 760 and 1440 wide, using the constants in e2e/helpers/responsive.ts.
The G4 QA agent runs the QA plan in the browser without reading the diff and records the videos; the PR shows them per check.
The FE guild owner reads the first 5 shadow results in the weekly report (G5-16) before asking for promotion.

"""RH-XXXX (example bug): a member's workgroup list shows a workgroup they don't belong to."""
from rest_framework import status

from rhinoCloud.rhinoCore.tests.test_factories.common_rhino_test_case import CommonRhinoTestCase
from rhinoCloud.rhinoCore.tests.test_factories.models.workgroup_test_factory import WorkgroupTestFactory
from rhinoCloud.rhinoCore.tests.unit_test_utils.list_response import get_uids_from_list_response


class WorkgroupListMembershipRegressionTestCase(CommonRhinoTestCase):
    def test_member_sees_only_their_own_workgroups(self):
        unrelated = WorkgroupTestFactory()  # fake data from the factories only

        response = self.primary_member_client.get("/api/v2/workgroups/")

        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, status.HTTP_200_OK)
        listed = get_uids_from_list_response(response)
        self.assertIn(str(self.primary_workgroup.uid), listed)
        self.assertNotIn(str(unrelated.uid), listed)  # fails on main, passes with the fix


# While working: ./scripts/local_run_backend_unit_tests.sh cloud rhinoCloud.rhinoCore.tests.views.test_rh_xxxx_workgroup_list

Only tests that run in the VM (unit tests and FCP Lab integration markers). Tests that need the QA envs go back to the BE guild with the evidence.
Done: the root cause in one line with file:line, and proveStable at 50 of 50 green, with the seed that used to fail included.

title: [DevOps] Infra upgrade fixer: repair failed provider, chart, Action bumps
needs: G7 DevOps checks and (stretch) the read-only plan on PRs; egress allow-list for the OpenTofu registry and chart repos via Nexus
what: When a Renovate PR in infrastructure or gitops fails its checks, repair our code for the new provider, chart or Action version, prove validate, tflint, trivy and kubeconform pass, and attach the CI plan when one exists.
why: Provider and chart updates are where infra drifts. The fixer does the reading and the mechanical edits; a person still reads the plan and applies.
how: Charter infra-upgrade-fixer, stage shadow, with the same walls as the pipeline fixer: no cloud credentials, never apply, destroy, sync or dispatch.

Checks run with no credentials (sketch, harness/scripts/verify-infra.sh, shipped with the harness; routines/ holds only data): tofu fmt, terragrunt hcl format, tofu validate per module with -backend=false, tflint, trivy config; for gitops, helm lint and helm template piped into kubeconform.
tofu init -backend=false and helm dependency build download providers and charts. Ask DevOps to serve them through Nexus or add the registries to the egress allow-list.
Provider majors: read the upgrade guide, search our modules, fix one module at a time, and list every resource the guide says may be replaced.
Plan: if G7's read-only plan job exists, link its output. Otherwise the PR says no plan was run and asks DevOps to run it before merging.

code.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ai-agents/harness/scripts/verify-infra.sh — sketch: checks that need no cloud credentials
set -euo pipefail
cd /work/infrastructure
tenv tofu install && tenv tg install            # versions from .opentofu-version and .terragrunt-version
tofu fmt --recursive -check=true
terragrunt hcl format --check
for module in modules/*/; do                    # validate modules directly: no backend, no state, no credentials
  tofu -chdir="$module" init -backend=false -input=false >/dev/null
  tofu -chdir="$module" validate -no-color
done
tflint --recursive                              # rules from G7's .tflint.hcl
trivy config --exit-code 1 --severity HIGH,CRITICAL modules/
if [[ -d /work/gitops ]]; then                  # gitops PRs: render every changed chart and check it
  for chart in $(git -C /work/gitops diff --name-only origin/main... | grep 'Chart.yaml$' | xargs -r -n1 dirname); do
    helm dependency build "/work/gitops/$chart"
    helm lint "/work/gitops/$chart"
    helm template "/work/gitops/$chart" | kubeconform -strict -ignore-missing-schemas -summary
  done
fi
# Never here: a plan with real state, apply, destroy or argocd sync. The plan comes from CI (G7) or a person.

why: Coverage numbers don't say whether tests catch bugs. A test that fails on a planted bug proves it does, and Meta's ACH had 73% of such tests accepted by engineers.
how: Weekly per area (frontend/src and cloud/rhinoCloud/rhinoCore), on recently changed code with low coverage (Vitest monocart coverage; coverage run in cloud-ci).

One writer proposes one merge. Proof: the existing tests and verify pass unchanged, and the PR shows the copies side by side.

title: [Platform] BE dead-code remover: vulture candidates, proven deletions
needs: G8 remove-dead-code skill
what: Reuse the FE dead-code flow for the cloud backend, with vulture as the finder and a verifier that knows the ways Django hides usage.
why: Unused backend code is harder to spot than FE code, because Django finds much of it by name. Proof per deletion keeps the PRs safe to approve.
how: Add a [tool.vulture] block to cloud/rhinoCloud/pyproject.toml (sketch). Start at confidence 80.

Django hides usage in URLs, admin, signals, Celery tasks (@app.task), DRF hooks, management commands, settings strings and the SDK's use of the API. The verifier checks each one; the SDK and the public API are never touched.
Same flow as G5-31: finders propose, the verifier proves, one writer deletes at most 10 items per PR, never add_code.
Before done: the cloud unit tests and makemigrations --check.

code.text:
# cloud/rhinoCloud/pyproject.toml — sketch of the [tool.vulture] block for the BE dead-code remover
[tool.vulture]
paths = ["rhinoCore", "rhinoTaskServices", "vulture_allowlist.py"]
exclude = ["*/migrations/*", "*/tests/*", "*/integration-tests/*", "*/rhino-containers/*"]
min_confidence = 80                 # start strict; lower it only if the verifier keeps up
ignore_decorators = [
    "@app.task",                    # Celery: app = Celery("rhinoCloud.rhinoCore.tasks") in celery_tasks/app.py
    "@receiver",                    # Django signals
    "@admin.register",
    "@action",                      # DRF viewset extra actions
    "@property",
    "@*.setter",
]
ignore_names = [
    "Meta", "get_queryset", "get_serializer_class", "perform_create", "perform_update",
    "has_permission", "has_object_permission", "to_representation", "validate_*",
    "handle", "add_arguments",      # management commands
    "setUpTestData", "setUp", "tearDown",
]
# vulture_allowlist.py lists names used only by URL configs, settings strings or the published SDK.
